$comment: EVERY `padding` FOUND ON A STYLE IN A RENDERED CONFORMANCE SUBJECT, sorted, per subject. The pin asserts the distinct set is identical and no value occurs less often — not the multiset, because a Card draws a header box AND a body box where a Surface drew one, so the COUNT necessarily grows on a conversion that changed no spacing at all. RE-CAPTURED BY F-214, WHICH IS THE PIN WORKING RATHER THAN THE PIN BEING EDITED AROUND: ten sites wrapped their content in a padded View inside a Surface that already pads, rendering 24pt where every call site read 12. Removing those boxes makes values occur less often, which is exactly what this refuses, so the capture is part of that feature and its numbers are in progress.md. F-210 captured the first version BEFORE converting 24 Surfaces into Cards; that baseline has done its job and is in the F-210 commit. Asserted by apps/mobile/test/screens.test.tsx. WHAT IT DOES NOT SEE: rhythm, and overflow. Equal insets are not the same screen. RE-CAPTURED BY F-227, and by arithmetic rather than by hand: the scales became the mockups own (ADR-0103), so every inset moved through the same snap rule as every reference — 12 to 8, 20 to 16, 28 to 24, 40 to 32, 56 and 96 to 48, everything else where it was. The 1 is the Swatch keyline and is not spacing. This file is the EXPECTATION, so moving it by the rule and letting the render check it is the honest direction: a screen whose padding did not follow the rule fails here. F-239 ADDED ONE SUBJECT AND CAPTURED IT RATHER THAN COPYING ITS SIBLING: screens/Preferences (a display switch off) renders the engine card with one row off, which is the state the sweep never saw — every other subject draws all three switches in their drawn state. Its eight 16s are the engine Card header and body on top of the six this screen already had; the sibling entry above still pins the six it was captured with, and the rule that a value may occur MORE often is why that entry did not have to move. F-233 REMOVED THE SWATCH WELL: the mockups draw no padded well around a sample, so each Swatch lost its 8-dp well padding — 427 occurrences across 44 screens, taken out of this pin by exactly that count and nothing else. F-233 REMOVED THE STRIP'S WELL AND RING: each Strip lost its 8-dp well and its 1-dp ring inset, 4 of each across 4 screens, and nothing else moved. F-234 REMOVED ONE VALUE, AND IT WAS NOBODY'S: each Lens subject's 10 — one in each of the twelve, and nowhere else — was gorhom's default handle padding (its handle container pads 10 all round), which reached the tree through the library's own handle. The sheet now draws 03's handle itself, 5 dp below the sheet's top with no padded box (ADR-0118), so the 10 is gone and nothing else moved. F-236 RE-CAPTURED FOUR SUBJECTS, each an empty state that offers a way elsewhere and is now drawn as 27's card, padded md (16) on every side (ADR-0128 §2): OutfitBuilder (nothing wearable), Shopping (no wardrobe at all), Export (nothing to export) and Wardrobe (nothing in it). And the Lens awaiting a capture now draws 27's working card, padded md (16), where a skeleton stood. Home (first run) draws its two absences — no readings and an empty wardrobe — as 27's cards: each was an engine Card with a padded header and body (two 16s), and is now one card padded md (16), so two 16s left the subject and no value did. F-236 ADDED EIGHT SUBJECTS, each the witness a screen’s declared condition needs (ADR-0129 §3), recorded as first captured: nothing matches on the Atlas, the phrase found nothing on the Finder, a colour this corpus does not hold on Compare, ColourCard, ColourDetail, Contemporary and Wear, and a capture the Lens refuses. F-240 ADDED ONE SUBJECT, the colour-vision preview’s label above the tab bar (ADR-0131 §5), recorded as first captured. Nothing else moved. F-240’S REVIEW (S2) RE-CAPTURED THE SIX PREFERENCES SUBJECTS: section 2’s card holds the colour-vision pills padded sm (8), 15’s measured inset, where it had copied a header and body padded md; 8 is the one value added to each, and the 16s each subject had gained since the capture (sections 2 and 3 as cards) are recorded as they are now. F-237 ADDED FOUR SUBJECTS, each captured through this test’s own capture() rather than typed: 06’s bookmark off and on (no padded box) and the Atlas bookmarked-only and none-bookmarked (the Atlas’s own values, fewer entries). F-238 ADDED TWO SUBJECTS, captured through this test’s own capture(): the Outfit Lab with every slot filled, with the save enabled and once saved (the Lab’s own values, its controls Surface padded as before). F-238 ALSO ADDED FOUR WARDROBE SUBJECTS, captured the same way: the lookbook choice, the lookbook, none saved, and an empty wardrobe with a saved outfit. Their 1.5 is new to this file and not new to the product: it is ChoiceGroup’s segmented inset, SEGMENT_INSET (2.5, F-232’s measured median) less the 1 dp edge, the first segmented group a screen subject draws. F-242 RE-CAPTURED HOME AND ADDED ONE SUBJECT, through this test’s own capture(), because Home was rebuilt to 01 and its padded boxes are 01’s: the hero, the wardrobe preview and the colour card, each a level-1 card padded md (16), and a 1 for the keyline of each sample that draws one (the hero, five tiles, the card’s sample). The reading block and its two engine cards are gone with ADR-0138, so values left the two existing subjects by design; the first run draws the hero, 27’s card and the colour card. The page inset (xl, ADR-0139) is the scroller’s contentContainerStyle and is not a style this walker reads. screens/Home (a wardrobe, no profile) is the E2 count without a profile. F-246 RE-CAPTURED THE ATLAS AND ADDED TWO SUBJECTS, through this test’s own capture(), because the Atlas was rebuilt to 05 and its padded boxes are 05’s: each card a level-1 card padded sm (8), 05’s 10 dp, and a 1 for each sample’s keyline. The 24 every Atlas subject carried was the frame’s own inset (lg); 05’s family row runs to the right edge and its grid to the tab bar, so the frame bleeds (Screen bleed) and each block pads itself in the list’s contentContainerStyle and its own Views’ paddingHorizontal, which this walker does not read — so the 24 left all four subjects by design, and the two empty subjects now record none. screens/Atlas (a season chosen) is the chosen pill’s form (ADR-0141); screens/Atlas (more filters open) is the overflow’s sheet (ADR-0143 D5), whose facets draw no padded box. F-247 RE-CAPTURED THE COLOUR PAGE, through this test’s own capture(), because the page was rebuilt to 06 and its padded boxes are 06’s: the readout, provenance and combinations cards, each a level-1 card padded md (16), and a 1 for each sample’s keyline the walker reads. The 24 and the 4 were the old page’s frame and hero insets: 06’s sample and names sit at md and its cards at xs, so the frame bleeds (Screen bleed) and each block pads itself with paddingHorizontal, which this walker does not read. The (sections folded) subject left with the accordion, and the two (06’s bookmark) subjects with the header bookmark (ADR-0147); the page is drawn whole, bookmarked, with an empty wardrobe and with nothing to rank (27’s card in the combinations’ place), and for the one entry outside sRGB.
